subsystems.name: Runtime instrumentation and profiling
subsystems.role: collects data on how the software performs and where time or memory is spent.

subsystems.name: Code representation and manipulation
subsystems.role: provides a structured, modifiable form of the program that the system can rewrite.

subsystems.name: Search and optimization engine
subsystems.role: generates candidate code changes and searches for better versions.

subsystems.name: Verification and validation
subsystems.role: checks that proposed changes are correct and do not break safety or functional requirements.
parts: formal verification tools (model checkers, theorem provers)

subsystems.name: Deployment and rollback
subsystems.role: safely replaces running software with improved versions and can revert if problems appear.

subsystems.name: Meta-level controller
subsystems.role: decides what to improve, when to run improvement cycles, and which methods to use.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the target software
buildSteps.detail: Add logging, metrics and profiling hooks so the system can measure execution time, memory use, and correctness signals.

buildSteps.title: Build a manipulable code model
buildSteps.detail: Parse the source into an abstract syntax tree or intermediate representation that can be programmatically edited and recompiled.

buildSteps.title: Define objectives and constraints
buildSteps.detail: Specify what 'better' means (e.g., faster, less memory) and hard constraints (e.g., must pass all tests, must satisfy safety properties).

buildSteps.title: Implement a search algorithm
buildSteps.detail: Use genetic programming or reinforcement learning to propose code mutations and recombinations that explore the space of possible programs.

buildSteps.title: Integrate automated verification
buildSteps.detail: For each candidate, run tests and formal checks; only changes that provably meet constraints are allowed forward.

buildSteps.title: Set up safe deployment
buildSteps.detail: Create a pipeline that can deploy a verified version, monitor it, and automatically roll back if it fails in production.

buildSteps.title: Add meta-level control
buildSteps.detail: Build a controller that chooses which modules to improve, allocates compute, and decides when human oversight is required.

buildSteps.title: Run iterative improvement cycles
buildSteps.detail: Repeatedly profile, propose, verify, and deploy, gradually improving the software while maintaining safety.

prerequisites.why: systems can fix simple bugs or generate small code snippets, but not rewrite complex architectures.
formal methods work on small, critical kernels; verifying large, evolving systems is beyond current capability.
genetic programming and neural program synthesis work on toy problems; searching real-world codebases is computationally prohibitive.
no proven way to guarantee that a self-rewriting system will not introduce subtle, dangerous flaws.
training and search require large amounts of compute, which is available but costly.
modern DevOps provides blue-green deployments and canary releases, but not for fully autonomous code changes.

pathway.milestone: Narrow automated program repair and genetic improvement in research and niche commercial tools
pathway.unlocks: faster bug fixing and performance tuning for well-defined modules.

pathway.milestone: Supervised self-improvement of specific performance-critical components under human review
pathway.unlocks: continuous optimization of isolated services without full autonomy.

pathway.milestone: End-to-end self-improvement of entire applications with formal safety guarantees
pathway.unlocks: software that can adapt to new workloads and hardware without human intervention.

pathway.milestone: Fully autonomous recursive self-improvement with open-ended capability growth
pathway.unlocks: rapid, continuous software evolution, but with major safety and control challenges.
